17:1.sourceText: Ταῦτα ἐλάλησεν Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶπεν Πάτερ, ἐλήλυθεν ἡ ὥρα· δόξασόν σου τὸν Υἱόν, ἵνα ὁ Υἱὸς δοξάσῃ σέ,
17:1.targetText: These things Jesus spoke, and lifted up His eyes to the sky, and said, “Father, the hour has come, glorify Your Son, that Your Son may also glorify You,

groups.note: Greek lifting participle is rendered as a finite lifted up clause in English.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds a second and before said; N1904 proceeds from the lifting participle to said without another conjunction.
LSV repeats Your before the second Son; the pinned N1904 has only the article at that occurrence.
LSV adds also before the Sons glorifying; no corresponding particle occurs there in N1904.

17:2.sourceText: καθὼς ἔδωκας αὐτῷ ἐξουσίαν πάσης σαρκός, ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκας αὐτῷ δώσῃ αὐτοῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
17:2.targetText: according as You gave to Him authority over all flesh, that—all that You have given to Him—He may give to them continuous life;

groups.note: The Greek genitive all flesh describes the domain of authority, expressed as over all flesh in English.

17:3.sourceText: αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ αἰώνιος ζωὴ, ἵνα γινώσκωσιν σὲ τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν καὶ ὃν ἀπέστειλας Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν.
17:3.targetText: and this is the continuous life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Him whom You sent—Jesus Christ;

17:4.sourceText: ἐγώ σε ἐδόξασα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, τὸ ἔργον τελειώσας ὃ δέδωκάς μοι ἵνα ποιήσω·
17:4.targetText: I glorified You on the earth, having completed the work that You have given Me, that I should do.

17:5.sourceText: καὶ νῦν δόξασόν με σύ, Πάτερ, παρὰ σεαυτῷ τῇ δόξῃ ᾗ εἶχον πρὸ τοῦ τὸν κόσμον εἶναι παρὰ σοί.
17:5.targetText: And now, glorify Me, You Father, with Yourself, with the glory that I had with You before the world was;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article nominalizes the world-being infinitival clause; English renders a finite before-the-world-was clause without a separate nominalizing article.

17:6.sourceText: Ἐφανέρωσά σου τὸ ὄνομα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις οὓς ἔδωκάς μοι ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου. σοὶ ἦσαν κἀμοὶ αὐτοὺς ἔδωκας, καὶ τὸν λόγον σου τετήρηκαν.
17:6.targetText: I revealed Your Name to the men whom You have given to Me out of the world; they were Yours, and You have given them to Me, and they have kept Your word;

groups.note: Greek aorist gave is rendered perfect You have given for the same giving event.
Greek they were to You expresses possession with a dative; English renders the whole relation they were Yours, keeping the copula and possessor together.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

17:7.sourceText: νῦν ἔγνωκαν ὅτι πάντα ὅσα δέδωκάς μοι παρὰ σοῦ εἰσιν·
17:7.targetText: now they have known that all things, as many as You have given to Me, are from You,

17:8.sourceText: ὅτι τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἔδωκάς μοι δέδωκα αὐτοῖς, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔλαβον, καὶ ἔγνωσαν ἀληθῶς ὅτι παρὰ σοῦ ἐξῆλθον, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.
17:8.targetText: because the sayings that You have given to Me, I have given to them, and they themselves received, and have known truly, that I came forth from You, and they believed that You sent Me.

groups.note: Greek aorist gave is rendered as English perfect You have given.

17:9.sourceText: Ἐγὼ περὶ αὐτῶν ἐρωτῶ· οὐ περὶ τοῦ κόσμου ἐρωτῶ, ἀλλὰ περὶ ὧν δέδωκάς μοι, ὅτι σοί εἰσιν,
17:9.targetText: I ask in regard to them; I do not ask in regard to the world, but in regard to those whom You have given to Me, because they are Yours,

17:10.sourceText: καὶ τὰ ἐμὰ πάντα σά ἐστιν καὶ τὰ σὰ ἐμά, καὶ δεδόξασμαι ἐν αὐτοῖς.
17:10.targetText: and all Mine are Yours, and Yours [are] Mine, and I have been glorified in them;

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplies the second nominal ownership clause; Greek omits a repeated are verb there.

17:11.sourceText: καὶ οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ εἰσίν, κἀγὼ πρὸς σὲ ἔρχομαι. Πάτερ ἅγιε, τήρησον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ᾧ δέδωκάς μοι, ἵνα ὦσιν ἓν καθὼς ἡμεῖς.
17:11.targetText: and I am no longer in the world, and these are in the world, and I come to You. Holy Father, keep them in Your Name, whom You have given to Me, that they may be one as We [are one];

groups.note: N1904 has the personal third-person plural pronoun they; LSV designates those same remaining people as these, with the deictic rendering explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

Source-witness relative/antecedent difference: N1904 has dative singular ᾧ referring to the Name given to Jesus, whereas LSV has personal plural whom referring to the people given. These different referents are left unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV has a personal people-relative here; N1904 has the singular which/Name-relative ᾧ. No false name-to-people relative link is supplied.
Bracketed English copula and one complete as We are one; N1904 has only as We at this final comparison.

17:12.sourceText: ὅτε ἤμην μετ’ αὐτῶν, ἐγὼ ἐτήρουν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ᾧ δέδωκάς μοι, καὶ ἐφύλαξα, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπώλετο εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ.
17:12.targetText: when I was with them in the world, I was keeping them in Your Name; I guarded those whom You have given to Me, and none of them were destroyed, except the son of the destruction, that the Writing may be fulfilled.

groups.note: Greek singular was destroyed agrees with none, while LSV uses were destroyed. The destruction predicate is retained with the English agreement difference explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
Source-witness relative/antecedent difference: N1904 has singular ᾧ referring to the given Name; LSV uses people-relative those whom. The different referents remain unpaired.
Greek and joins the Name-giving clause to I guarded; LSV rearranges the people-relative as the guarded object and has no corresponding conjunction at this point.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds the world-location phrase to when I was with them; pinned N1904 has no such phrase in this verse.
LSV makes the given people the object of guarded; N1904 has singular which referring to the given Name. The actual keeping object them stays linked to its own earlier occurrence.

17:13.sourceText: νῦν δὲ πρὸς σὲ ἔρχομαι, καὶ ταῦτα λαλῶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἵνα ἔχωσιν τὴν χαρὰν τὴν ἐμὴν πεπληρωμένην ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.
17:13.targetText: And now I come to You, and these things I speak in the world, that they may have My joy fulfilled in themselves;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

17:14.sourceText: ἐγὼ δέδωκα αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον σου, καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἐμίσησεν αὐτούς, ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου καθὼς ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου.
17:14.targetText: I have given Your word to them, and the world hated them, because they are not of the world, as I am not of the world;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

17:15.sourceText: οὐκ ἐρωτῶ ἵνα ἄρῃς αὐτοὺς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου, ἀλλ’ ἵνα τηρήσῃς αὐτοὺς ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
17:15.targetText: I do not ask that You may take them out of the world, but that You may keep them out of the evil.

review.note: The Greek substantival evil expression can be read evil/the evil one; LSV prints the evil. The mapping preserves that displayed wording without deciding the interpretive referent.

17:16.sourceText: ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου οὐκ εἰσὶν καθὼς ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου.
17:16.targetText: They are not of the world, as I am not of the world;

17:17.sourceText: ἁγίασον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ· ὁ λόγος ὁ σὸς ἀλήθειά ἐστιν.
17:17.targetText: sanctify them in Your truth, Your word is truth;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds possessive Your to the first truth phrase; N1904 has an article without a possessive there. The actual second possessive σός belongs to Your word.

17:18.sourceText: καθὼς ἐμὲ ἀπέστειλας εἰς τὸν κόσμον, κἀγὼ ἀπέστειλα αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν κόσμον·
17:18.targetText: as You sent Me into the world, I also sent them into the world;

17:19.sourceText: καὶ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἐγὼ ἁγιάζω ἐμαυτόν, ἵνα ὦσιν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἡγιασμένοι ἐν ἀληθείᾳ.
17:19.targetText: and I sanctify Myself for them, that they also may be sanctified in truth themselves.

groups.note: The Greek personal/intensive plural αὐτοί supplies both subject and emphasis, split in English as they ... themselves; these are not two independent source pronouns.

17:20.sourceText: Οὐ περὶ τούτων δὲ ἐρωτῶ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ τῶν πιστευόντων διὰ τοῦ λόγου αὐτῶν εἰς ἐμέ,
17:20.targetText: And I do not ask in regard to these alone, but also in regard to those who will be believing in Me through their word,

groups.note: N1904 has a present believing participle; LSV renders it prospectively as will be believing. The believing predicate is shared with that English future interpretation explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

17:21.sourceText: ἵνα πάντες ἓν ὦσιν, καθὼς σύ, Πατήρ, ἐν ἐμοὶ κἀγὼ ἐν σοί, ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἡμῖν ὦσιν, ἵνα ὁ κόσμος πιστεύῃ ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.
17:21.targetText: that they all may be one, as You Father [are] in Me, and I in You, that they also may be one in Us, that the world may believe that You sent Me.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplies the nominal You-Father-in-Me clause; no Greek copula is written there.
LSV repeats one in the second that-they-may-be clause; the pinned N1904 has only may be in Us at that point.

17:22.sourceText: κἀγὼ τὴν δόξαν ἣν δέδωκάς μοι δέδωκα αὐτοῖς, ἵνα ὦσιν ἓν καθὼς ἡμεῖς ἕν·
17:22.targetText: And I have given to them the glory that You have given to Me, that they may be one as We are one—

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in as We are one; Greek writes as We one without a finite copula.

17:23.sourceText: ἐγὼ ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ σὺ ἐν ἐμοί, ἵνα ὦσιν τετελειωμένοι εἰς ἕν, ἵνα γινώσκῃ ὁ κόσμος ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας καὶ ἠγάπησας αὐτοὺς καθὼς ἐμὲ ἠγάπησας.
17:23.targetText: I in them, and You in Me, that they may be perfected into one, and that the world may know that You sent Me, and loved them as You loved Me.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds and before the second purpose clause that the world may know; N1904 begins that clause directly with ἵνα.

17:24.sourceText: Πατήρ, ὃ δέδωκάς μοι, θέλω ἵνα ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ κἀκεῖνοι ὦσιν μετ’ ἐμοῦ, ἵνα θεωρῶσιν τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἐμὴν, ἣν δέδωκάς μοι ὅτι ἠγάπησάς με πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
17:24.targetText: Father, those whom You have given to Me, I will that where I am they also may be with Me, that they may behold My glory that You gave to Me, because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.

groups.note: N1904 uses neuter singular collective what You have given Me, whereas LSV uses personal plural those whom. Here both describe the given people as the following they also makes clear; the collective/personal-number wording difference is explicit, unlike the Name-relative difference in 17:11–12.
N1904 perfect have given is rendered English simple past You gave for the same giving act.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

17:25.sourceText: Πατὴρ δίκαιε, καὶ ὁ κόσμος σε οὐκ ἔγνω, ἐγὼ δέ σε ἔγνων, καὶ οὗτοι ἔγνωσαν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας·
17:25.targetText: Righteous Father, also the world did not know You, and I knew You, and these have known that You sent Me,

groups.note: Greek aorist knew is rendered English perfect have known for the same knowledge event.

17:26.sourceText: καὶ ἐγνώρισα αὐτοῖς τὸ ὄνομά σου καὶ γνωρίσω, ἵνα ἡ ἀγάπη ἣν ἠγάπησάς με ἐν αὐτοῖς ᾖ κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτοῖς.
17:26.targetText: and I made known to them Your Name, and will make known, that the love with which You loved Me may be in them, and I in them.”

groups.note: The Greek accusative relative reprises the love as the cognate object of loved; English expresses that relation instrumentally as with which. The same love relation is retained with its grammatical recasting explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
